chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), that he said:
"The will (testament) is a right upon every Muslim."

key_terms.اَلْوَصِيَّةُ: The will or testament; the act of bequeathing property or instructions after death.
key_terms.حَقٌّ: A right; something obligatory or due.
key_terms.مُسْلِمٍ: Muslim; one who submits to God.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on making a will for Muslims?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi cites this chain to establish the *wasiyyah* (will) as a fundamental right (*haqq*) incumbent upon every Muslim, reflecting the Shia emphasis on fulfilling financial and spiritual obligations to heirs and the poor. This ruling underscores the legal necessity of estate planning to ensure the proper distribution of wealth according to divine law, preventing disputes among heirs.
